description:
Flaccy plays the music you own at full quality: FLAC, ALAC, WAV, AIFF, MP3 and AAC. A native Mac app with a real equalizer, gapless playback, synced lyrics you can share as a video, Last.fm scrobbling and a menu bar player. No account, no ads, and your files never leave your Mac.

SEE EXACTLY WHAT YOU'RE HEARING
• Codec, bit depth and sample rate on every track, from CD quality to Hi-Res
• Gapless playback that honors your albums (exact for lossless files), with a queue that survives relaunches
• A built-in Listening Guide that explains what Bluetooth, wired DACs and your Mac really deliver. No snake oil

A REAL EQUALIZER
• Drag the curve and hear it change, or switch to Advanced for up to ten bands with bells, shelves, filters and adjustable Q
• 16 presets and your own. Import Equalizer APO and AutoEq profiles to tune for your headphones
• A separate setting for every output: AirPods, a wired DAC, the speaker. Flaccy switches when you do
• Automatic headroom keeps boosts from clipping, and Hold to compare is level-matched, so louder never sounds better
• Keyboard-first: arrows move a band, ⌥⌘E opens it from anywhere
• Works with every format and keeps playback gapless. Off or flat, the signal passes through untouched

YOUR LIBRARY, ORGANIZED
• Index your music folder in place: no copying, no locked-in library format
• Folder watching: files you add appear instantly, and messy folder names and scene releases are identified and cleaned up automatically (AI cleanup is included in the trial and in Lifetime)
• Albums, artists, songs and playlists with search, multi-column sorting and large artwork
• Duplicate songs are listed once, and Flaccy builds smart playlists from your own listening

MADE FOR THE MAC
• Liquid Glass design built natively for macOS
• Media keys, a menu bar mini player and Control Center Now Playing
• Keyboard-first: play, love, queue and search without touching the mouse
• Drag-and-drop import and right-click everything
• Synced lyrics that fill in word by word when a song has word timing, with click-to-seek and a timing control for songs that run off
• Share Lyrics: pick the lines you love and get a short video of them over the song itself, in four looks and four formats for Stories, posts and more
• AirPlay, a sleep timer and an immersive Now Playing view with lyrics and queue side by side
• Zoom the whole window with ⌘= and ⌘-
• Six themes that change the colors, type and cover shapes, and four ways to see your albums: grid, wall, list or carousel

YOUR SERVER, TOO
• Play from Navidrome, Flaccy Server or any OpenSubsonic server, over your home network or Tailscale
• Songs stream without filling your Mac and download for offline when you want them
• One purchase covers iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch

SCROBBLE EVERYTHING
• Sign in with Last.fm and every play is scrobbled, even offline, with automatic retry
• Listening charts, a listening clock and artist bios matched to your library
• Year in Music: shareable story cards and a poster of your listening year, exportable at full resolution

REDISCOVER YOUR COLLECTION
• Home picks up where you left off, with mixes made from your own listening and what you played on this day in years past
• Start a station from any song: Flaccy builds a queue from your own library
• Suggested playlists, similar-artist trails, and a wantlist for the albums you're hunting
• Share any track as a universal streaming link while you keep your FLACs

TRY IT FREE
Flaccy is free for 7 days from the first time you play your own music. After that, keep everything with a one-time Lifetime purchase, or choose the yearly plan. The yearly plan renews automatically unless canceled at least 24 hours before the end of the period; manage or cancel it in your Apple Account settings.

Flaccy plays FLAC, ALAC, AAC, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF and CAF.

Terms of Use: https://mako.midgarcorp.cc/terms/flaccy
Privacy Policy: https://mako.midgarcorp.cc/privacy/flaccy
whatsNew:
Flaccy 2.0.

Flaccy opens 2.0 with a short look at everything it can do. Here is what is new on the Mac.

THEMES
Six themes change how all of Flaccy looks: its colors, its type, the shape of its covers and how Albums is laid out. Phosphor is green on black in a monospaced face, Liner Notes is paper with serif titles, Hi-Fi cuts its covers round, Gallery is a wall of covers, Marquee shows one cover at a time, and Flaccy is the look you know.
Albums has four views now: a grid, a wall of covers, a list and a carousel. Each theme picks one, and the switch beside Sort changes it.
Your own cover shape, corners and font sit over whichever theme is on, and you can copy any theme to change it: a theme is a folder holding one text file, and what you save in it shows in the window a moment later.
Themes are in Settings under Appearance.

SETTINGS
The Settings window is laid out like System Settings: a sidebar with a search and a page for each area. The search reads every label and control.

CLEAN LIBRARY
One switch, Clean Library, replaces Hide Duplicate Songs and Group Album Editions. Every song is listed once, wherever its copies live: on this Mac, on a server, or under another artist credit on the same album.
Clean Up Library keeps to the songs in your library folder and leaves a server's songs alone.

PLAYLISTS, REMASTERED
A removal or a drag is one step that Edit > Undo, or the Undo on its toast, takes back.
Songs the library has lost keep their places, and Remove Missing Songs takes them out.
Suggested Songs from your own library sit under every playlist.
Add to Playlist skips songs a playlist already holds, lists the playlists you added to last first and checks the ones that hold the songs.
The playlists list can play a playlist next, add it to the queue or copy it.

YOUR SERVER
When a server has songs this Mac also holds, Flaccy offers to free up the space or keep them downloaded. Plays, loves, playlist places and song volume stay with each song.
Download Quality in Settings › Servers: Original File, AAC 256 kbps or AAC 128 kbps.
Once a server is added, an Offline chip in the Library keeps the songs that play with no server in reach.
A large server's library fills in while its first sync is still reading.
Music added to your server shows up as soon as you open Flaccy.
Sheets that open by themselves, such as the summary after a first sync, now appear when Flaccy is in the background too.

ALSO
Home opens on the page it kept, and a large library is back about twice as fast.
Albums of MP3 and M4A files are listed in track order again.
If your free trial ended a month or more ago, Flaccy gets a second look: seven more free days, starting when your own music plays.
Flaccy now sends anonymous crash reports beside its usage counts, so I can fix what breaks. Settings › About › Usage Counts shows exactly what is sent and turns it all off with one switch.
